_what_this_file_is: The divergences between direct execution and execution under .LEXE that are
INTENDED, each with the clause that makes it intended. against_lexe.py
refuses to load an entry that has no reason and no citation, because a
forgiven divergence without a written reason is a blind spot wearing a green
Every entry here was MEASURED FIRST and attributed afterwards. None was
predicted. Where an attribution could be proved rather than argued, the proof
is a second deliberate pass named in the reason -- run it and the specimen
passes, which is what makes the claim 'this is the cwd / the environment /
the network permission and nothing else' true rather than plausible.
A `token` is `<kind>:<key>`. When `actual` is present the entry forgives only
that value: a DIFFERENT value under the same key is still a finding.

Re-attributed for cab0a5e: sealing / and /etc, and the honest dependency refusal, both changed the value these entries pin. That is the mechanism working -- the change surfaced as a FAILURE and was attributed by hand.

linux-env-declared-present.reason: The runtime clears the caller's environment and sets only an allowlist, so a variable the caller exported is not visible to the application. Format 0.1 has no manifest field by which a package could request an environment variable, so there is no conforming way for this specimen to receive one.
linux-env-declared-present.citation: docs/ISOLATION.md, 'Environment policy'; docs/FORMAT-0.1.md 5.7 (the closed list of optional manifest fields contains no environment)

linux-env-declared-present.reason: As above: the environment is cleared, so an exported empty-valued variable is absent rather than empty.
The specimen prints the hex and length of a variable only when it is present; with the environment cleared these keys are correctly not emitted.

linux-env-unicode-value.reason: The environment is cleared; a UTF-8 valued variable is as absent as any other.
Emitted only when the variable is present.
Emitted only when the variable is present.

The runtime gives the application a private data root at $HOME and $LEXE_APP_DATA instead; the private data/cache/temp roots ARE writable, which the passing filesystem specimens show.

linux-fs-readonly-probe.reason: The sandbox seals `/` and `/etc` read-only, so the write is DENIED exactly as the baseline had it -- the behaviour matches and only the mechanism differs. Direct execution was denied by file permission (EACCES); the sandbox denies by read-only mount (EROFS). The same denial, reported by a stronger mechanism. This replaces an earlier entry that forgave only /usr and deliberately left /etc and / FAILING, because at that time they were writable -- which is what this file is for: the value is pinned, so when the behaviour changed the entry stopped matching and had to be re-attributed by hand instead of absorbing the change silently.
linux-fs-readonly-probe.citation: docs/ISOLATION.md, 'Filesystem view'; docs/REFERENCE-POLICY.md (the sandbox seals / and /etc read-only as of cab0a5e)

linux-fs-cwd-relative-asset.reason: The runtime sets the working directory to the application's private data root, never to the directory the payload lives in and never to the caller's cwd, so a relative path to an asset shipped in the package does not resolve. PROVEN to be the working directory and nothing else: with --stage-into-data, which places the same asset in the data root where the cwd actually is, this specimen PASSES.
linux-fs-cwd-relative-asset.citation: docs/ISOLATION.md, 'Writable roots' ('The working directory is the private data root -- never the caller's cwd'). NOTE: docs/FORMAT-0.1.md 9 does not specify the working directory at all; that gap is reported separately.

linux-fs-cwd-relative-asset.reason: Consequence of the above: the open fails rather than returning wrong data.

The specimen's own self-check reports that its environment did not behave as it requires, which is accurate: the cwd is not where its asset is. Forgiven ONLY on this specimen and ONLY for this value, because the cause is a documented runtime decision that the same specimen's --stage-into-data pass isolates.

linux-socket-name-resolution.reason: /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf are bound into the sandbox only when the `network` permission is granted, and this pass grants nothing. PROVEN: with --grant-network this specimen PASSES, as do all five sockets specimens.
linux-socket-name-resolution.citation: docs/ISOLATION.md, 'Filesystem view' ('resolv.conf/hosts only when networking is permitted'); docs/FORMAT-0.1.md 5.7.1 (`network` is the enforced permission)

linux-socket-name-resolution.reason: getaddrinfo cannot resolve `localhost` without the NSS host configuration, which is withheld with the permission.
Not emitted when the lookup failed.
The specimen reports the resolver's error code only when the lookup failed. Which failure a resolver reports is environment-dependent -- the corpus itself records that, having been bitten by it.
linux-socket-name-resolution.citation: docs/ISOLATION.md, 'Filesystem view'; tests/workloads/README-PE.md, fixture mismatch 3 (the same code is environment-dependent)

linux-socket-name-resolution.reason: With no resolver configuration the bogus name fails with EAI_AGAIN rather than EAI_NONAME. That it FAILED is the property; which code says so is not, and the corpus says as much.

linux-link-rpath.reason:
NOT a runtime defect, and now reported honestly. This specimen's DT_RPATH/DT_RUNPATH is the ABSOLUTE path of its build directory, so the binary runs only from where it was built; the supported pattern is a $ORIGIN-relative rpath. Two independent confirmations that the property, not the runtime, is the obstacle: linux-link-origin-relative PASSES, and a $ORIGIN-built variant of THIS specimen's own source runs identically under .LEXE (measured -- so symbol versioning itself is covered even though this specimen cannot cover it). What changed: the runtime records the dependency contract at install and refuses the launch with a stated reason and a repair hint, instead of exec'ing into a silent exit 127 whose loader message was discarded. Exit 1 is 'an unexpected failure' per REFERENCE-POLICY 3.
REPORTED SEPARATELY, and deliberately not forgiven anywhere: the same mechanism OVER-triggers on a package whose library the sandbox could satisfy from /usr. against_lexe_lifecycle.sh carries the regression check for that.
linux-link-rpath.citation: examples/native/bundled-library/Makefile (the documented pattern is -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN/../lib'); docs/REFERENCE-POLICY.md 3 (exit codes)

linux-link-rpath.reason: The launch was refused before the program started, so there was no program output to deliver. This is NOT the relay defect, which is fixed: a program that does run now has both streams delivered on every exit code, verified byte for byte over 8 MiB including NULs.

linux-link-three-libs-ldpath.reason: This binary has no RPATH at all and found its libraries through LD_LIBRARY_PATH, which the runtime deliberately does not forward -- and FORMAT-0.1 9.5.2 now REQUIRES not forwarding it. The runtime refuses the launch honestly, with a dependency-contract diagnostic, rather than exec'ing a binary that cannot start. A genuine positive.
linux-link-three-libs-ldpath.citation: docs/FORMAT-0.1.md 9.5.2 (the environment MUST NOT forward LD_LIBRARY_PATH); docs/REFERENCE-POLICY.md 3

linux-link-three-libs-ldpath.reason: The launch was refused, so there was no program output.

linux-proc-daemon-double-fork.reason: A console-mode launch is bounded by the sandbox: when the process the runtime waited for exits, the sandbox is torn down and the detached daemon dies before it can finish its work. PROVEN to be the launch mode and nothing else: with --launch-mode service the same specimen leaves daemon.log behind, which is what Format 0.1 5.6 requires of a service ('the application MUST survive the process that started it'). Console-mode behaviour is not specified either way; that gap is reported separately.
linux-proc-daemon-double-fork.citation: docs/FORMAT-0.1.md 5.6 (service semantics); docs/ISOLATION.md, 'Privilege / process creation' (--die-with-parent, private PID namespace)

linux-proc-orphan.reason: Same as linux-proc-daemon-double-fork: the orphaned child does not outlive the console-mode sandbox. With --launch-mode service it does, and orphan.log appears.
